The ''' 1936 [[German football championship]]''', the 29th edition of the competition, was won by [[1. FC Nürnberg]] by defeating [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] 2–1 after extra time in the final. It was Nuremberg's sixth championship and its first since 1927. Fortuna Düsseldorf made its second final appearance, having previously won the competition in 1933 but, after 1936, the team would never appear in the final again. Nuremberg had eliminated the champions of the previous two seasons, [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] in the semi-finals, making 1936 the only final from 1933 to 1942 not to include the club. Schalke however would return to its winning ways the following season when it defeated Nuremberg in the 1937 final.<ref name="List" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duitchamp.html |title=(West) Germany -List of champions |website= Rsssf.com |access-date= 31 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/1-fc-nuernberg/1/  |title= 1. FC Nürnberg » Steckbrief |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 31 December 2015|language=de|trans-title=1. FC Nürnberg honours}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/fortuna-duesseldorf/1/  |title= Fortuna Düsseldorf » Steckbrief |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 31 December 2015|language=de|trans-title=Fortuna Düsseldorf honours}}</ref>

[[PSV Chemnitz]]'s [[Erwin Helmchen]] was the top scorer of the 1936 championship with ten goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/deutsche-meisterschaft/ |title=Deutsche Meisterschaft » Torschützenkönige |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 2 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=German championship: Top goal scorer}}</ref>

It was the last German championship final in [[Berlin]] to be played at a venue other than the [[Olympiastadion (Berlin)|Olympiastadion]], the latter having been built for the [[1936 Summer Olympics]] and being used for all finals from 1937 to 1944 and six more after the [[Second World War]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/spielorte/olympiastadion-berlin/3/ |title=Olympiastadion, Berlin (Deutschland) » Historische Spiele|website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 31 December 2015|language=de|trans-title=Olympic Stadium Berlin, historic games}}</ref>

The sixteen [[1935–36 Gauliga|1935–36]] [[Gauliga]] champions competed in a group stage of four groups of four teams each, with the group winners advancing to the semi-finals. The two semi-final winners then contested the 1936 championship final. The 1936 season saw the introduction of a game for third place, played between the two losing semi-finalists.<ref name="Rsssf" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duithistpre45.html |title=German championship 1936 |website= Rsssf.com |access-date= 31 December 2015}}</ref>
